correctness.rationale: Exact conditional comparison probabilities follow from uniform rank placement among k+1 intervals. The selected-selected and unselected-unselected pairs are handled separately, yielding the precise sum over j of j(k-j) interior gaps. Optimization is a finite nonnegative-gap linear program with all n-k slack; symmetry of weak compositions gives uniform-mixture expectation, and the Radon-Nikodym density identity gives covariance. Exact rational checker on every uniform permutation for n=2..7 and all marked sets confirms the four identities and sharp boundaries, with independent n=8,k=4 hand values. No infinite claim relies on enumeration.

value.rationale: The selected-position mixture is a natural partial randomization construction in Pinsky's work. An exact per-gap cost j(k-j)/(k+1), a complete sharp range and equality layouts identify where preserving order has greatest inversion effect for every size and marked-subsequence length, including growing k. The global negative covariance follows without relying on an ad hoc fixed-length table. The specific positions and their exact optimization are essential to the question rather than arbitrary parameter slices.
